newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA NAMPO URGES GOVT ACTION ON POULTRY IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA NAMPO URGES GOVT ACTION ON POULTRY IMPORTS.

text.p: South Africa's National Maize Producers Organisation (Nampo) on Monday called on the government to protect the local poultry and maize industries against the impact of cheap broiler imports.
Giel van Zyl, Nampo's general manager said in a statement that each tonne of imported meat replaced around two tonnes of yellow maize, which is used for animal feed.
"Over 12 months these imports replace around 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize which could have been used domestically to the benefit of both poultry producers and maize farmers," van Zyl said.
"This could contribute towards stronger economic growth, job creation and save valuable foreign exchange."
Nampo noted that the central Reserve Bank recently reduced its 1997 economic growth forecast to 2.0 percent from 2.5 before, mainly due to a slowdown in the agricultural sector.
"A 25 percent reduction in the country's growth rate is dramatic and should be prevented," van Zyl said.
He said that South African importers were bringing in, both legally and illegally, more than 10,000 tonnes of chicken meat every month, despite a possible oversupply of yellow maize this year.
South Africa's embattled poultry industry and the country's poultry importers have long been fighting a war of words over the need for protective tariffs.

The poultry industry, which last year asked government to raise tariffs on imports to 64 percent from 27 percent currently, has in the past blamed traders for skirting tariffs to illegally bring in cheap broilers. Traders say the industry is badly managed and inefficient.
